It looks like the newly renovated Freedom Plaza is getting even more new statues. The one on horseback was planned, but there are now a dozen more statues lining the northern and southern edges of the plaza.





— https://nitter.net/maustermuhle/status/2057836357322502617#m

Ron Paul (@RonPaul)

President Trump had choice: 

- Retire the Empire gracefully (stop the wars, close the foreign bases, and bring all the troops home) 
- Or give the Empire another puff of oxygen.

He chose the latter, against the wishes of the American people.

But this time Trump has poked a stick at the wrong hornet's nest, and is trapped.

With every passing day, the costs escalate, and the American people feel increased economic pain. 

It's now well past the time to retire the Empire ..
And if you stop by to see Simon, post a picture!

I put “ordinary” in quotes because really there’s no such thing. If you want to learn more about the “ordinary” soldiers of the Revolution this Memorial Day weekend, listen to some of their stories here: piped.video/z5yUisX9H88?si=YcWd…

The installation includes a group of statues: “ordinary” Revolutionary soldiers from all manner of backgrounds now adorning Freedom Plaza near the White House during the 250th anniversary of our country.
It was dark and rainy, so I’ll have to fly back to get a better picture and a closer look at the other soldiers. The whole installation, even in the rain and the dark, was extremely moving.

The way I learned of it was wild, even providential: I happened to be in D.C. for a dinner, and someone associated with the statues gave me a tip to walk over to the plaza later that night and pay special attention to the first statue off the truck.

There are lots of statues of famous Revolutionary War heroes in Washington, D.C.

Now there’s a monument to one of the countless unsung heroes—and he happens to be my great-great-great-great-great grandfather, Simon Knowles!
